If the player is killed whilst in darkened Anor Londo, they are returned to the first bonfire regardless of whether they have rested there or not. Whether it is a glitch or an intended function by the developers is unconfirmed.

title: Deep Accursed
snippet: The Deep Accursed in Anor Londo is visible on the ceiling in the grand hall and will drop down when the player tries to reach the switch to open the main doors. The pillars can be used as cover. However, a safer strategy is to retreat up one of the staircases and slay it from a distance. Whilst the beast cannot reach the player, it will frequently jump into the air to reposition itself, and can cause damage if the player is too close. If the player remains out of its sight long enough, the monster may calm down again, allowing them to resume the fight with a plunging attack.

title: Anor Londo (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Anor Londo (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : Unlike its Dark Souls counterpart, Anor Londo's illusionary shining sun is gone and has been replaced with the cold blue rays of the moon. The city has noticeably frozen over, as well as being severely reduced in size, with the only remaining parts of the old city being the cathedral, the rotating staircase, and the honorary tomb of Gwyn. An additional tower now stands where the entrance of the building housing the Painted World of Ariamis once stood, with an invisible walkway leading to the top. Additionally, only three of the Silver Knights remain and all Batwing Demons are gone. The cathedral has been overrun by Deacons of the Cathedral of the Deep and Writhing Rotten Flesh. The inside of the cathedral has been covered in corpses and maggots. The eastern section of the cathedral has been blocked off by debris, but the western section is still accessible and contains the body of an old blacksmith.

title: Berenike Knight
snippet: As the First Flame began to fade, countless among the ranks of the Berenike Knights became Undead and ventured to Lordran. Here they tried to make their way toward Anor Londo through the only possible access: Sen's Fortress. The knights of Berenike and Tarkus thus entered the dangerous proving ground; after decades of struggling to advance, much of the Knights ended up as Hollows, becoming a threat to the other Undead in the location. Tarkus, probably accompanied by some fellow knights, eventually reached the peak of Sen's Fortress and challenged the last trial in the form of the Iron Golem. The mighty knight in black iron armor managed to defeat the guardian of Anor Londo, gaining access to the city of the gods. However, after reaching Anor Londo, Tarkus perished at the hands of the Painting Guardians before he could reach Gwynevere and obtain the Lordvessel. The few Berenike Knights that followed him to Anor Londo ended up inside the Painted World of Ariamis.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet:
Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight -  Dark Souls III - character - plot 
 plot : Upon meeting with Gwynevere for the first time, she grants the player the Lordvessel, which enables the ability to warp between most bonfires. Gwynevere can also initiate players into the Princess's Guard covenant.

Killing Gwynevere, which requires a single hit with any attack, will reveal that she is an illusion created by Gwyndolin. Gwyndolin then removes the rest of his enchantment, causing the sun to permanently set in Anor Londo. In addition, any player that darkens Anor Londo will become more susceptible to Blade of the Darkmoon invasions when human. All deaths within Anor Londo will return the player to the first Bonfire in Anor Londo by the Darkmoon Knightess, regardless of the last bonfire used. In addition, all regular enemies will vanish, except Painting Guardians, a few Silver Knights and two new hostile characters.

title: Darkmoon Knightess
snippet:
Darkmoon Knightess -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : The Darkmoon Knightess is one of Dark Sun Gwyndolin's loyal followers and the fire keeper of the first bonfire in Anor Londo. As with the other fire keepers, the Darkmoon Knightess can upgrade Estus Flasks using Fire Keeper Souls. Like all other fire keepers, killing the Darkmoon Knightess will cause the fire she watches over to be extinguished, although players can still warp to it after obtaining the Lordvessel.

Should the player kill Gwynevere, the Darkmoon Knightess will appear directly in front of the elevator of Anor Londo to offer punishment for the deed. Should the player attack Dark Sun Gwyndolin, the Darkmoon Knightess will also become hostile and reside in her usual location, the first Anor Londo bonfire. Her armor, the Brass Set can be found in the room with the sunlight blade miracle after defeating Dark Sun Gwyndolin.

title: Sen's Fortress
snippet: Centuries after Lord Gwyn's sacrifice, as the First Flame began to fade and the curse of Undeath to regain strength heroes and warriors from all different lands tried to reach Lordran and ventured to Sen's Fortress to try and reach Anor Londo. Very few were successful, like the strongest Berenike Knight known as Black Iron Tarkus and a Warrior of Sunlight known as Solaire of Astora. title: Astora
snippet: The country of Astora is heavily influenced by the culture of the gods of Anor Londo and subservient to their ideal of continuing the Age of Fire through the sacrifice of a Chosen Undead. The legend of the Chosen Undead is known to Astoran nobility, including the family of Oscar, an Astoran knight who travelled to the Northern Undead Asylum in order to free an Undead who could then make pilgrimage to Lordran and link the fading Flame. Solaire of Astora, an adherent of the cult of Gwyn's firstborn, finds himself in Lordran in his quest to reach Anor Londo; Undead Prince Ricard of Astora had the same goal, but went hollow before he could reach the city. Anastacia of Astora serves as the Firekeeper of Firelink Shrine and Andre of Astora serves as a blacksmith in the Undead Parish, both of them welcoming the Undead that arrived at Lordran in search of Flame.

The Cathedral of the Deep enslaved most of the known surviving giants, forcing them to protect their interests in the Cathedral, Irithyll Dungeon, and occupied Anor Londo. The Giant Sentinels in the city of gods were likely reduced to the disgraced, unclad beasts found sleeping on the way to the old Cathedral of Anor Londo, a line of defense against those intruding on Aldrich. The Greatarchers of Hawkeye Gough went nearly extinct, save one atop a tower in the Undead Settlement who guarded the White Birches found around the foot of the High Wall. Gough himself is remembered for having struck down a calamitous dragon with his Greatbow during the events of *Dark Souls*.

title: Gods
snippet:
Gwynevere, Goddess of Sunlight and eldest daughter of Gwyn. She fled Anor Londo prior to the events of *Dark Souls*, after which she married the God Flann, with whom she had several children. By the time of *Dark Souls III*, she married King Oceiros, making her the Queen of Anor Londo's neighbouring kingdom of Lothric, and mothered three of his children, although she has fled this kingdom too by the events of the game.
Gwyndolin, God of the "Dark Moon" and of the "Dark Sun", and lastborn son of Gwyn. Raised in secrecy as a girl, he is a hybrid likely mothered by Crossbreed Priscilla, and the last God left in Anor Londo and Lordran by the events of *Dark Souls*, although he remains perceived as somewhat of a minor deity, acting from the shadows, including by creating an illusion of Gwynevere. By the events of *Dark Souls III*, he succeeded Lloyd as ruler of the Gods, and reigned from Irithyll, their new seat of power he built atop old Anor Londo.

title: Anor Londo (Dark Souls III)
snippet: In the times of the kingdom of Lothric, things have changed. The beautiful city that once had a glowing sunlight is now cold and dark; the cathedral where the Chosen Undead once fought Ornstein and Smough is now corrupted by the Deep and the home to Gwyndolin, who took his father's title of King of the Gods but fell ill; and the chamber that once held Gwynevere now has nothing but the Sun Princess Ring. A denizen that came from the Painted World, Sulyvahn, infiltrated the city of Irithyll and Gwyndolin's Covenant and later proclaimed himself Pontiff. When Gwyndolin fell ill and became incapable of leading the city and the Covenant, he was forced to retire in the cathedral. The leadership passed to Captain Yorshka, Gwyndolin's crossbreed sister, who was immediately imprisoned by Sulyvahn. Sulyvahn converted Irithyll's knights to the worship of the Deep. The Pontiff then led his master and Saint of the Deep, Aldrich, to devour the helpless Gwyndolin.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - overview 
 overview : Blade of the Darkmoon is considered one of the more difficult covenants to master. Every person the player invades as a spirit of vengeance has likely had experience in PvP (since Indictments during an invasion are one of the few repeatable ways of gaining sin), and so will usually put up a tougher fight than people invaded by Darkwraiths. To make matters worse, people in Dark Anor Londo are likely to be duel-mongerers who kill Blades of the Darkmoon for sport or for souls. They very often have friendly summons with them.

However, the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant is very worthwhile. The Darkmoon Talisman has the best miracle adjust in the game, so any player who relies on miracles would benefit from joining this covenant; in turn, Darkmoon Blade is an excellent weapon buff. With patience and perseverance, players may yet reap the benefits of the Blade of the Darkmoon.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - activities 
 activities : Blades of the Darkmoon hunt players that have attacked the illusion of Gwynevere or have committed any amount of sins by either getting kicked out of a covenant or being indicted by other players. Players risk nothing invading other people's worlds (cannot be indicted and all souls and humanity are kept upon death) and gain a Souvenir of Reprisal for each guilty player they defeat.

Outside of Gwyndolin, the only character part of the covenant is the Anor Londo Fire Keeper, although she does not provide a fellow Darkmoon Blade with anything besides unique dialogue. Attacking Gwynevere or passing through Gwyndolin's fog gate will result in her turning hostile, but killing the Fire Keeper will not count as betraying the covenant.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Dark Sun Gwyndolin -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Gwyndolin is the lastborn child of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and one of the deities who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire, although his legitimacy as such only came from being a child of his father. He was worshipped as the "God of the Darkmoon" and held the title of "God of the Dark Sun".

Despite being the son of Gwyn, Gwyndolin was born with a strong moon power, and "weak and repulsive" in appearance, particularly due to the snakes coiled around his lower half. Because of his darkmoon powers and his strong affinity for moon magic, as well as his lineage, Gwyndolin was raised as a female. While still young, Gwyn made him wear women's clothing and gave him a magic ring which would allow Gwyndolin to move and act in a feminine way, leading him to behave "like a dark and fleeting goddess".

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Cut content from *Dark Souls III* reveals that it was possible to obtain a consumed finger of Gwyndolin, presumably after defeating Aldrich, and give it to Yorshka for her to keep as a memento.
In *Dark Souls*, 末子 is translated to lastborn, but in *Dark Souls 3* it is instead translated to its more accurate meaning of youngest son in the Darkmoon Ring description. This can call the canonicity of lastborn into question, as the difference doesn't exist in the original JP.
Gwyndolin is a derivative of the Welsh name "Gwendolyn" meaning "white ring"
**Among her namesakes, the legendary Queen of Britain Gwendolyn is particularly well-known, as depicted in "*Historia Regum Britanniae*" by Geoffrey of Monmouth, one of the oldest historiographers and authors of Arthurian Legend. Gwendolyn was renowned for her wisdom and grace in these tales.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Dark Sun Gwyndolin -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategies 
 strategies : Gwyndolin's boss battle takes place in a seemingly never-ending corridor.

He is not a very difficult boss if the player has decent dodging skills. Of his three attacks, two can be avoided by hiding behind pillars, while the last one is more powerful and fast (he will tend to use the Sphere Shot after Orb Spread if the player is hiding behind pillars). The main issue in this fight is reaching him, as he will teleport away when the player approaches (equipping the Ring of Fog may increase the time available to attack before he teleports), meaning that the best time to run up to him is when he is just finishing off his Arrow Spread, as he takes a few moments to recover. Gwyndolin can still be damaged while he is in his teleporting animation and for a split second after actually moving, so it is possible to deal considerable damage at that moment.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Both the Orb and Arrow Spread attacks are avoidable by hiding behind one of the pillars on either side of the corridor. The Sphere Shot, on the other hand, will go through walls, inflicting full damage if not blocked or avoided. The Orb Spread and Sphere Shot are Magic-based, though, so a shield that can block 100% physical damage and has good Magic resistance, like the Crest Shield, is recommended for this fight.

While devastating, both the Sphere Shot and Arrow Spread attacks have no tracking whatsoever and are easily avoided simply by running diagonally. If a player does not want to risk it too much, a good strategy to catch up to him is by moving from pillar to pillar until they are about two pillars away from Gwyndolin and then wait until he shoots his Arrow Spread. This attack can consist of two-to-four arrow barrages. Wait until he finishes the second one and go for him, if he shoots any subsequent arrows, dodge them by running diagonally.

 theories : It is possible to theorize that Gwyndolin is the result of the union of Gwyn and Crossbreed Priscilla for several reasons:
**Gwyndolin is the last child of Gwyn; but Yorshka, a half-dragon, is his younger sister, confirming that they share a mother. Since the two siblings both possess draconic traits, their common mother should have possessed draconic traits herself for them to inherit them partially.
**Gwyndolin, despite being another children of Gwyn, did not inherit the power of Sunlight like the rest of his father's lineage. Instead he inherited the magic of the moon that made him a powerful moon sorcerer, a power that was unique to the white dragon Seath, the probable father of Priscilla.
